description: Foundation entries for an embodiment-neutral Blacklight Continuum d10 system. The rules measure what a character can do, not what kind of body, substrate, species, or origin they possess.

entries.title: Blacklight Original d10 System Foundation
entries.summary: An original Attribute-plus-Skill d10 framework supporting operatives, supernatural archetypes, advanced technology, Exposure, equipment, investigation, social conflict, and dangerous field operations without assigning mechanics by body type.
body: Build a test pool from Attribute + Skill + situational modifiers. Results of 6 through 9 produce one success. A 10 produces one success and may activate a specialization, equipment quality, or power rider. A failed roll containing one or more 1s creates a Complication.

Difficulty normally ranges from one to five successes. Characters may Push by rerolling failed dice up to Resolve, then gain Exposure representing accumulated risk, cognitive strain, supernatural attention, operational instability, or psychological pressure according to the scene.

The core rules never grant or deny abilities because a character is biological, synthetic, transferred, copied, transformed, embodied, disembodied, or otherwise instantiated. A capability exists only when an Attribute, Skill, Archetype feature, power, equipment item, condition, or explicit narrative permission says it exists.

Appearance, physiology, species, substrate, and embodiment remain character and setting details. They do not create free armor, senses, immunity, movement, damage, healing, or access. Those benefits must be purchased or recorded as capabilities in the same way for every character.

The current rules remain an alpha foundation. Combat, advancement, power trees, equipment, and character-sheet interfaces are active development areas, but embodiment neutrality is a permanent system principle.

entries.title: Capability Framework
entries.summary: All extraordinary effects are defined by capabilities, costs, limits, and outcomes rather than by body origin, species, substrate, or presumed anatomy.
body: A capability is anything a character can reliably attempt beyond ordinary untrained action: a supernatural power, professional technique, technological interface, ritual, transformation, resistance, special sense, movement mode, social authority, or other explicit permission.

The rules ask what the capability does, what pool activates it, what it costs, how long it lasts, what resists it, and what happens on failure. The rules do not ask whether the effect comes from blood, training, mutation, magic, machinery, spirit, faith, memory, code, or an unusual physical form unless the individual capability makes that source mechanically relevant.

Two characters may describe the same mechanical capability through entirely different origins. Conversely, two characters with similar appearances or origins gain no shared mechanical benefit unless both possess the appropriate capability.

Archetypes organize thematic capability families. Operational Frames organize learned professional competence. Equipment provides external capabilities. Conditions temporarily add, restrict, or alter capabilities. None of these require a universal theory of the character's body.

entries.title: Character Creation Foundation
entries.summary: Characters are built from identity, Attributes, Skills, Operational Frame, Archetype, powers, limitations, relationships, equipment, and explicit capabilities rather than an assumed physical template.
body: Define the operative before Q-MAP or before the campaign's inciting transition, including their Blacklight role, one relationship, one mission memory, and one reason they accepted transmission or displacement.
Assign one Attribute at 4, three at 3, three at 2, and two at 1. Assign three Skills at 3, five at 2, five at 1, and the rest at 0. Choose three specializations.

Choose an Operational Frame, an Archetype, three identity anchors, one defining capability, one meaningful limitation, starting powers according to the campaign's allocation rules, and two statements defining the character's relationship with Charles.

Describe the character's appearance, species, embodiment, transformations, or substrate freely, but record every rules-relevant benefit as an Attribute, Skill, power, equipment feature, innate ability, or condition. Description alone does not grant mechanics.
keyFacts: Identity anchors can be people, places, promises, habits, moral boundaries, sensory memories, fears, failures, or reasons for loyalty and distrust.
Each character begins with one memory of the final Q-MAP moments that contradicts another character's account.
The core system is compatible with biological, synthetic, supernatural, transferred, copied, transformed, and other forms of character embodiment.
What matters mechanically is the capability recorded on the sheet.

entries.title: Equipment and Salvage Foundation
entries.summary: Equipment is defined by quality, function, tags, limits, and access rather than by compatibility with a presumed body type.
body: Equipment quality ranges from Improvised through Serviceable, Professional, Advanced, and Exceptional. Better quality improves reliability, adds dice in a defined role, or changes what actions are possible.

The team initially obtains equipment from maintenance tools, emergency stores, damaged compartments, recovered technology, fabrication systems, remote manipulators, and incomplete memories of familiar devices.

Items must state a clear operating effect, quality, tags, limitations, interface requirements, and resource dependence. A character can use an item when they possess the required capability, training, access, or adaptation; the system does not assume compatibility from anatomy or species.
When equipment requires a particular interface, size, environment, authority, or support system, record that restriction explicitly as a tag instead of hiding it inside body lore.
